title: Stirling PDF
wrapper_note:
the upstream init script creates symlinks under /usr/local/bin and needs root;
TOS forbids root containers, so this wrapper starts the unmodified Spring Boot
jar directly as uid 1000 on 8080, with configs/logs/storage/pipeline/customFiles
mounted writable.
descript: Stirling PDF is a locally hosted PDF toolbox: merge, split, rotate, compress, OCR, convert, watermark, sign and more, all from a web UI. Files are processed on your NAS and are not sent to a third party. This package runs the official Docker Hub image as a non-root container and keeps settings and working data in the application data folder.
release_note: 1. First release: Stirling PDF 3.3.0 from Docker Hub, x86_64 + aarch64, non-root.
important: Open the web UI and use the tools directly; login is disabled by default. Settings live in DockerAppData/stirlingpdfdocker/configs, working data in .../data. Large PDFs and OCR need RAM/CPU; the first start can take 1-2 minutes. Needs DockerEngine; add a registry mirror if Docker Hub is unreachable. Back up configs before uninstalling with data removal. Plain HTTP on the LAN.

data_notes: `configs` holds application settings and templates; `data` is the working data folder used by the PDF pipelines. Uploaded files are processed inside the container and are not kept as a permanent library unless you save them.
design_notes: **Rootless Spring Boot.** `src/entrypoint.sh` starts `/app/app.jar` directly as uid 1000 on 8080; the upstream init script is bypassed because it needs root.
**Two volumes, one port.** `/configs` + `/data`; only 8080 is published.
**Health check** probes `/` on 8080; the first start can take 1-2 minutes.
**Fixed image tag**, Docker Hub only, no privileged mode, no host network, no Docker socket.
limitations: No login is enabled by default. Anyone who can reach the published port can use the tools; do not expose it to the internet without a TLS reverse proxy and, if needed, enable security.
OCR and large PDFs are CPU/RAM intensive. Very large jobs may need a bigger container memory limit.
Uploaded files are processed transiently; this is not a document management system. Keep your originals elsewhere and download the results.
